negative_findings.description: No evidence of a national/domestic card scheme (a Macedonian-branded card scheme with its own scheme rulebook) was found. Searches in Macedonian for 'национална картична шема / домашна картична схема' returned nothing; CaSys appears as a processor and card-system operator for international schemes (Visa/Mastercard) rather than a domestic brand owner.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cell hypothesis of a 'national card scheme' is unsupported by evidence found in this pass.

brief: For North Macedonia, the payments rule-setting layer is a three-body structure: NBRSM (owner/operator of the MIPS RTGS and overseer of everything else), KIBS AD Skopje (bank-owned clearing house running retail deferred-net clearing plus the domestic instant-payments platform, and an eIDAS trust service via OneID), and CaSys / Интернационален картичен систем (domestic card processing and card-system operation). The genuinely public, versioned rulebook is the NBRSM 'Правила за работа на МИПС'; KIBS exposes little more than a single operating-rules PDF and no visible tariff or admission-criteria page, and CaSys publishes almost nothing rule-shaped, so operator rules for retail clearing and cards must largely be inferred from NBRSM oversight documents, the National Payment System Council, banking-association bulletins and diffed bank general terms and conditions. The live deadline pressure in this cell is external: SEPA geographical accession (EPC approval March 2025, operational readiness from October 2025) and the Banca d'Italia-led TIPS Clone connection targeted for 2026, both of which will convert into participant-facing migration mandates. Practical constraint for collection: nbrm.mk returns 403 to naive fetchers, so the whole backbone of this cell needs browser-grade retrieval.
